In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterisation of molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) for nia and their use as recognition system for nicotinamide molecules.
the synthesis of molecularly imprinted microsphere for the selective recognition of nia.
the preparation of microspheres by precipitation polymerization and with the characterization of the resulting imprinted microspherical particles by SEM, NMR and DFT studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of MeCN, the imprinted activity is reduced, probably due to the competition between solvent and template molecules to interact with the functional monomer.
the imprinted activity of MAA-nia microspheres is strongly affected by the solvent employed during polymerization and re-binding processes.
the use of MeCN during polymerization and re-binding process can lead to a loss of imprinted activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the imprinted microspheressynthesized in chloroform are more selective towards nia analogues than those obtained in MeCN.
we have developed an effective method for the preparation of molecularly imprinted microsphere for nicotinamide molecules.
the use of MeCN as incubation solvent for the re-binding experiments is not recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of chloroform as incubation solvent for the re-binding process can improve the recognition ability of imprinted microspheress.
the use of chloroform as polymerization solvent is crucial to prepare imprinted microspheresshowing high affinity and selectivity towards the template molecule.
the choice of the solvent is critical for the synthesis of imprinted materials with good selectivity and re-binding capacity.
